neighbours.label: a verb of belief or imagination in an embedded clause, as in 'what I thought was impossible' or 'anything you can think of', as against verbs of saying or knowing
fire: She finally finished what she thought was an endless project.
Pack every snack you can think of for the long drive.
We found the key in a drawer we thought was empty.
Invite anyone you can think of to the opening night.
He climbed what he thought was the highest peak in the range.
The police had good reason for believing the story was false.
Try every colour you can think of before you paint the wall.
They reached what they thought was the end of the tunnel.
quiet: She finally finished what her boss said was an endless project.
Pack every snack you have bought for the long drive.
We found the key in a drawer we knew was empty.
Invite anyone you have met to the opening night.
He climbed what the guide said was the highest peak in the range.
The police had good reason for saying the story was false.
Try every colour you have at home before you paint the wall.
They reached what the map showed was the end of the tunnel.
